# Model Configuration Reference

<!-- This file is auto-generated by `composer docs:config`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every constraint below is read from `SchemaBuilder`, which the config validator
also consumes. Where a rule lives in the consuming code — meta field types, relationship
cardinalities, field permission operations — the schema reads it rather than keeping a copy,
so this document cannot describe a rule the framework does not enforce.

---

## `type` (required)

Model type. Post type aliases resolve to "post", taxonomy aliases to "taxonomy".

Accepted values:

`post-type`, `cpt`, `posttype`, `post_type`, `taxonomy`, `tax`, `category`, `cat`, `tag`

---

## `name` (required)

Model name, subject to WordPress database column limits.

| Model type | Maximum length |
|---|---|
| Post type | 20 characters |
| Taxonomy | 32 characters |

---

## `active`

Whether to register this model. Defaults to true when absent.

> **Warning:** Truthy non-true values (1, "yes") are treated as false and disable the model.

---

## `labels`

Display strings for the post type or taxonomy.

Recognized keys under `labels.overrides.ui`:

`enter_title_here`

Any other key under `overrides.ui` is inert and warns.

---

## `meta`

Meta boxes and fields. Each box key must have "fields" or "sections", not both.

### Box keys

| Key | Notes |
|---|---|
| `data_type` | Serialization strategy: "serialize" stores all fields under one key; "unserialize" stores each separately. Accepted: `serialize`, `unserialize`. |
| `register_rest_api` | Expose to REST. Must be strict true; truthy non-true values are treated as false. |
| `fields` | Field list. Mutually exclusive with "sections". |
| `sections` | Grouped fields. Mutually exclusive with "fields". Each section must have its own "fields". |

### Field types

44 types are recognized. The map passes through the
`saltus/framework/meta/matched_fields` filter, so a site may add its own — which is why an
unrecognized type warns rather than erroring.

`accordion`, `background`, `backup`, `border`, `button_set`, `callback`, `checkbox`, `code_editor`, `color`, `color_group`, `content`, `date`, `datetime`, `dimensions`, `fieldset`, `gallery`, `group`, `heading`, `icon`, `image_select`, `link`, `link_color`, `map`, `media`, `notice`, `number`, `palette`, `radio`, `repeater`, `select`, `slider`, `sortable`, `sorter`, `spacing`, `spinner`, `subheading`, `submessage`, `switcher`, `tabbed`, `text`, `textarea`, `typography`, `upload`, `wp_editor`

---

## `relationships`

Named relationships between models. Each relationship requires "type", "model", and optionally "reciprocal".

Accepted cardinalities:

`has_one`, `has_many`, `belongs_to`, `many_to_many`

---

## `features`

Feature opt-ins. Unknown feature names are silently ignored.

| Section | Accepted keys | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend` | `template`, `callback` | Public frontend rendering. Accepts "template" or "callback". |
| `blocks` | `variations`, `callback` | Gutenberg block registration. Accepts "variations" or "callback". |
| `drag_and_drop` | — | Post-list reordering capability declaration. Only read by permission policies; no runtime handler. |
| `draganddrop` | — | Admin UI for drag-and-drop reordering. Separate from "drag_and_drop" — they are not aliases. |

---

## `webmcp`

Browser-driven MCP proposals. Accepts "enabled", "policy", "tools", "editorial_review".

`enabled`, `policy`, `tools`, `editorial_review`

---

## `ai_context`

AI context generation via /wp-json/saltus/v1/ai-context/. Accepts "enabled", "policy", "fields".

`enabled`, `policy`, `fields`

## Taxonomy-only keys

### `associations`

Post types this taxonomy applies to. Taxonomy-only; raises an error on a post type.

### `supported_post_types`

Post types this taxonomy applies to. Same effect as "associations".

---

## Known top-level keys

Every key a model may declare at depth 0. Anything else warns with a nearest-match
suggestion. Note that `register_post_type()` arguments are **not** top-level keys — they are
read from `options` only, so a top-level `public:` or `hierarchical:` really is inert.

`active`, `admin_cols`, `admin_filters`, `ai_assistant`, `ai_context`, `associations`, `block_editor`, `blocks`, `description`, `draganddrop`, `duplicate`, `editorial_review`, `features`, `frontend`, `labels`, `mcp`, `meta`, `name`, `options`, `privacy`, `quick_edit`, `relationships`, `remember_tabs`, `settings`, `single_export`, `slug`, `supported_post_types`, `supports`, `type`, `webmcp`, `wp_cli`

## Validating a config

```bash
wp saltus config validate
wp saltus config validate --format=json
```

Exits non-zero when any model has an error. Warnings do not fail the command and do not
stop a model registering — an existing site must not break because a key it has used for
years is now spelled differently.

Validation also runs at registration, and the `/health` endpoint reports the verdict under
`config` so a broken config is visible without CLI access.
